details: CONFIRMED by a scratch test (reproduced with the new code, passes with master's lib). lanes_state builds
changed = {lane.branch: touched(main, default, lane.branch, trees.get(lane.branch))} from the list _one_lane_per_train returns; the rider
lanes are replaced by Lane(train, None), so the riders' worktrees are never read for modified files. The same happens in the start brief's
"files they have changed" list (line 395). The worktree half of touched() was there exactly for uncommitted work; the change silently loses it
for riders. A rider being worked on after it was merged into a train is the red-train fallback the delegate skill describes.
evidence: new code:    running [('wt/train-1', None)] picks ['z'] waits []        -> 1 failed
master lib:  running [('wt/a', 'a')] picks [] waits [Wait(slug='z', file='lib/z.py', branch='wt/a')]  -> 1 passed
failing_case: wt/a (item a, own commit lib/a.py) merged into wt/train-1; the rider's worktree then has an uncommitted change to lib/z.py (a fixer at work
after a red train, or a check fix); open item z with where lib/z.py.
Now: running [wt/train-1 (None)], z is picked (picks ['z'], waits []): z starts and collides with the edit in wt/a.
Before the change (master): running [wt/a], z waits (Wait z, lib/z.py, wt/a). Should: z waits on lib/z.py.
fix_hint: Keep the riders' files in the overlap map: compute touched() for each original running lane (or let _one_lane_per_train return the riders per
train) and attach the riders' files to the train lane; or count a rider whose worktree is dirty as its own lane.
pass_cases: 1. The failing case: z is in waits with file lib/z.py (branch wt/a or wt/train-1), not in picks.
2. wt/a, wt/b merged into wt/train-1, no uncommitted edits, setting 2: running is one lane, free 1 (today's new test keeps passing).
3. An open item whose where names lib/a.py (committed by the rider) waits while the train is open.
4. A rider with no train and an uncommitted edit to lib/z.py: z waits on wt/<rider> (unchanged behaviour).
reason: tests/test_lanes_state.py test_f1_rider_uncommitted_edit_still_blocks_overlap and test_f1_committed_rider_file_blocks_while_train_open pass; first fails on old lib.
findings.summary: a rider's uncommitted edits drop out of the overlap check: the lane becomes the train, and touched() reads the train's worktree, not the rider's

details: CONFIRMED by reading: heads is every refs/heads/wt/ ref; the only filter on the train is `not landing(...)`, which is always false for a ref
that holds a running rider (see notes). Nothing tells a live train from an abandoned one. Measured live: 3 leftover train refs, and
wt/relay-plugins (not landed) is an ancestor of all three, so if it becomes active again through worktree edits it shows as lane "wt/train-19".
The pre-existing rule for no-item worktrees already uses lane_quiet_hours for exactly this question; the train is not held to it.
evidence: git for-each-ref refs/heads/wt/ -> wt/train-19, wt/train-20, wt/train-22 present; merge-base --is-ancestor <train> master -> no for all three
git merge-base --is-ancestor wt/relay-plugins wt/train-19|20|22 -> yes, yes, yes
git worktree list -> .worktrees/train-19, train-20, train-22 still present
failing_case: Train wt/train-1 with riders wt/a and wt/b goes red; per the delegate skill they fall back to landing one at a time (a fixer on wt/a,
wt/b waiting to land). The train's ref and worktree are left (live today: wt/train-19, wt/train-20, wt/train-22 all exist, none on master,
worktrees still present). Setting 2: now 1 of 2 running (the dead "wt/train-1", slug None), one more item starts; the line names a train
nobody builds. Should: the train is no longer being landed, so wt/a and wt/b count as 2 of 2.
fix_hint: Treat a holding branch as an open train only when it is active within lane_quiet_hours (_activity on the train's ref and worktree), and prefer
the most recently active one when several hold the rider; otherwise the rider counts as its own lane.
pass_cases: 1. Riders wt/a, wt/b in wt/train-1 whose last activity is older than lane_quiet_hours (or that is otherwise marked dead): 2 of 2 running, free 0.
2. Riders wt/a, wt/b in an active wt/train-1 (changed within lane_quiet_hours): 1 of 2 running, free 1 (the item's failing case).
3. A train waiting 110 minutes for a paid run (activity 110 min old, quiet hours 3): still one lane.
4. A rider wt/a held both by a dead wt/train-19 and a live wt/train-23: it is counted under wt/train-23, not wt/train-19.
reason: tests/test_lanes_state.py test_f2_dead_train_does_not_fold_riders, test_f2_rider_counts_under_the_live_train_not_the_dead_one, test_f2_train_waiting_110_minutes_is_still_one_lane pass; first two fail on old lib.
findings.summary: any leftover wt/* branch that holds a rider counts as an open train: a dead (red, abandoned) train still folds its riders into one lane

details: CONFIRMED by measurement. In the generator, relay_git.has_own_commits(main, lane.branch) (a reflog read) is re-evaluated for every head,
then two merge-base --is-ancestor calls per head; for a lane with no own commits it is still called once per head. Project principle 2
(Waste): waste that repeats on every run is MEDIUM and is fixed before the merge.
evidence: for 3 runs: new 3.79 / 3.85 / 3.79 s, master 1.81 / 1.85 / 1.86 s (PYTHONPATH=<code>/plugins/front/lib:<code>/lib, lanes_state('/Users/amidman/relay'))
failing_case: Live repo, 3 running lanes, 11 wt/* refs: lanes_state takes 3.79-3.85 s with the change vs 1.81-1.86 s on master (3 runs each); 61 of its
109 git calls come from _one_lane_per_train. The lanes hook runs it on every UserPromptSubmit and every Stop of the front, with a 10 s timeout;
at 6 lanes and more leftover refs it grows as lanes x refs x 2. Should: about one git call per running lane (or fewer).
fix_hint: Per running lane: skip it at once unless has_own_commits (once); then one `git for-each-ref --contains refs/heads/<lane> --format=%(refname:short) refs/heads/wt/`
gives the holding refs; drop the always-false landing() call.
pass_cases: 1. Live-like fixture (3 lanes, 11 wt/* refs, no rider): _one_lane_per_train makes at most one git call per running lane plus one for-each-ref.
2. The item's failing case still gives 1 of 2 running, free 1.
3. A rider not yet in the train still counts as its own lane.
reason: tests/test_lanes_state.py test_f3_one_ref_scan_per_rider_candidate passes (26 calls on old lib vs <=2).
findings.summary: Waste on every front hook: has_own_commits and is-ancestor run per lane per wt/* ref, doubling lanes_state time (1.85 s to 3.8 s live)
